slides.heading: Sort K Sorted Array
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Heaps
slides.narration: Let's solve Sort K Sorted Array, a hard heaps problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Every element is at most k positions from its sorted position; sort with a size-(k+1) min-heap.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Every element is at most k positions from its sorted position; sort with a size-(k plus 1) min-heap.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Every element is within k of its spot, so the minimum of the next k plus one items is always next in order.
slides.narration: Every element is within k of its spot, so the minimum of the next k plus one items is always next in order.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Min-heap of size k + 1 → O(n log k)
slides.narration: A full sort ignores the structure. Since each element is at most k away from its spot, the smallest of the next k plus one elements is always next, so a heap of size k plus one gives n log k.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Fill a min-heap with k plus one items
slides.narration: Step by step. First, fill a min-heap with k plus one items. Second, pop the min into place. Third, push the next item. Fourth, drain the heap.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Add 3
slides.narration: Push 3. The heap isn't full yet.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Add 1
slides.narration: Push 1. The heap isn't full yet.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Add 5, pop 1
slides.narration: Push 5. The heap has more than 3, so pop the smallest, 1, which must be in its final place.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Add 7, pop 3
slides.narration: Push 7. The heap has more than 3, so pop the smallest, 3, which must be in its final place.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Add 6, pop 4
slides.narration: Push 6. The heap has more than 3, so pop the smallest, 4, which must be in its final place.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Drain the heap → sorted
slides.narration: Drain the rest of the heap. The array is sorted.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We push each element, and once the heap exceeds k, poll into the next write slot. Then drain the heap.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log k. Space is O of k.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: With k zero it's already sorted.

bullets: Every element is within k of its spot, so the minimum of the next k plus one items is always next in order.
